intro.title: Build schema to type mapper
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a TypeScript utility that automatically generates TypeScript type definitions from a simple data schema object. You will learn how to use TypeScript's mapped types and conditional types to transform schema keys and values into corresponding type properties. The main constructs involved are generic types, keyof, and template literal types. By the end, you'll have a reusable type mapper that ensures your data structures are type-safe based on your schema.
intro.usecase: This pattern is essential when building dynamic form builders or configuration panels where schemas define UI structure and validation rules. For example, in dashboard builders like Grafana or form tools like Formik, schemas describe field types, labels, and constraints, which must be mapped to TypeScript types for type-safe data handling. Developers use schema-to-type mappers to ensure that user inputs match expected structures, preventing runtime errors in data processing. This approach is also common in API clients that generate types from OpenAPI schemas, enabling autocomplete and validation in IDEs.
